## Delegation (Claude Code)

This section is rendered by the AgentKit plugin ( `{{PLUGIN_URL}}` ). Change the rules there, then re-run `init.sh`; repo-specific rules go outside the markers.

AGENTS.md's Autonomy section, done with Claude Code's tools. The plugin's `factory` skill is the loop; verify command of this repo: `{{VERIFY}}`.

- Start follow-up tickets yourself with the Agent tool, in the background, not as prompts for {{OWNER_NAME}} to paste into new sessions. Use Opus
  for large milestones and Sonnet for small, well-specified ones. Give the
  agent the ticket, its branch, worktree and port; when it reports back, review its result ( the ticket's checks, `{{VERIFY}}` ) before merging.
- Set each agent's reasoning effort explicitly ( the Agent tool's `effort` ): `high` for builders by default,
  `xhigh` for foundations that later work builds on ( a new API, coordinate maths ), `medium` for small mechanical
  tickets on Sonnet. A plan may set it per milestone; that wins. An orchestrating
  session itself runs at `high` and raises it only for a real judgement call ( reviewing an API, a milestone that missed its target ).
- Before starting one, check ListAgents: don't duplicate a session {{OWNER_NAME}} already opened. A peer session's transcript is
  `~/.claude/projects/{{TRANSCRIPT_DIR}}/<session id>.jsonl` ( read-only ): read its end to tell finished from waiting for an answer.
- Subagent prompts must say "assume and record under **Assumptions** in the ticket, don't ask" ( AGENTS.md, Autonomy: assumptions over questions ); read each builder's assumptions in review and list them in your report to {{OWNER_NAME}}.
- Keep the orchestration state outside the conversation: a queue memo ( running builders with ports, worktrees and tickets; the queued tickets in dependency order; which tickets must not run at the same time because they edit the same files ) in memory or a scratch file. The conversation may be compacted at any time; everything else lives in the tickets and on the branches.
- Wait with Monitor ( the plugin's `scripts/watch.sh`, a script that prints a line per change: a card moving, a transcript going quiet ), never by polling in a loop. A Monitor expires; re-arm it when it does.
- Subagents pause when the account's usage window is exhausted ( HTTP 429 ): their state is on their branch. Resume each with SendMessage once the window has reset; do not restart them.
- Subagents end with the session that started them: for work that must outlive it, start a separate session.
